page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-128GB is a General Purpose cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10% with a score of 788.68. However, multi-core performance is significantly stronger, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 23432.45 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 18317.0, which is in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly at 255.76 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only large block speeds at 90.98 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 41.03 GB/sec. Cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities are strong, as shown by PassMark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which contributes to the lower single-core performance metrics. Despite this, the high core count and 128.0 GB memory capacity offer a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources. It is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and general-purpose web serving. It is less suitable for single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing for 70B models drops to a weak 6.61 tokens/sec.
